text:
The Oilers are 16-3-3 with 35 points, the best record in this group, and five straight wins. Connor McDavid took a 21-game point streak into Philadelphia and kept it going. Under Mike Babcock, hired in June, the results have been everything Edmonton could want.

The process is another matter, and it's the story of the season so far. Edmonton has taken 49.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 48% at five on five, and just 42% during this five-game run. It has scored 22.9 more goals than its chances deserve, by far the biggest gap in this group, and our playoff model rates it about 10.8 points luckier than its play. The McDavid and Leon Draisaitl line with Vasily Podkolzin is the real thing: 61% of the chances and 22 goals for against 6. The problem is depth. The Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels line is at 30% and has been outscored 11-5, and Oilersnation is already asking where help up front comes from.

The goaltending is carrying the gap. Tristan Jarry is .951 with 9.8 saved above expected over his last five starts, and Devon Levi has won five straight. That's the question to watch: how long two hot goalies can cover a team that's even on the ice. A 98% playoff chance means it may not matter much in April.
